minutes_text:
INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

The Arts Commission meeting was held on Wednesday, July 21, 2021, via Zoom. Commissioner Metcalf called the
meeting to order at 6:33 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Aletha Metcalf, District 1
  Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District 3
  Commissioner Vicki Banks, District 4
  Sabrina Barnes, Director, Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department
  Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Onna Ehrlich-Bell, District 2

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Banks made a motion to approve the minutes from April 17, 2021. Commissioner Metcalf
seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Banks and Metcalf
  Nays: Commissioner Battle

Quarterly Report/Check-in Regarding Hollywood Park/SoFi Stadium Public Art

  Jason Witt, Director of Community Engagement from Hollywood Park/SoFi Stadium gave a quarterly update
report regarding Hollywood Park/SoFi Stadium Public Art stating there is a signed agreement for two (2) of Allison
Sar’s sculptures Summer and Carefree, two (2) 8-feet bronze statues that will be installed in the retail section and
completed early in 2022. Mr. Witt went on to say talks have begun regarding the installation of art inside the YouTube
Theater, a 6,000 seat performance venue scheduled to be opened in September 2021. As things develop, updates
will be provided. Sabrina Barnes asked about the commitment status of Inglewood Artist (whose name escaped her
mind) but one of her pieces consists of a water piece on the wall and another piece. Mr. Witt answered he believes
the artist does have an executed agreement but he would still need to verify with the team. Mr. Witt stated that there
are various water pieces to select from artist Coletta Rauls.

  1
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

  Sabrina Barnes provided Jason Witt with an outline (from the previous Arts Commission Meeting) of the Arts
Commission’s recommendations for commissioning Inglewood Artists for the Hollywood Park, LLC
Commitment/Expenditure agreement of $2 million that states the Inglewood Arts Commission is specifically tasked by
the Project Development Agreement (PDA) to “consult” with Hollywood Park Developers, LLC to inform and select
the public art commissions, displays and purchases of works directly from Inglewood artists, with program allocations
of a minimum of $2 million in percent for art funds from Hollywood Park. Per the Project Development Agreement
Exhibit E – Amendment and Restatement: ‘the art contributions can be aggregated and used to fund larger and more
impactful art and art facilities such as a museum or iconic architectural feature of the Stadium creating a singular
project identity, and a minimum of $2 million shall be dedicated to the commission, acquire and/or display public art
directly from local Inglewood artists. The selection of such local art shall be made in consultation with the Inglewood
Arts Commission.’ Stating although the Art Commission does not have its typical authority to review and comment on
the developer’s public art plans, public art works, art sites, art budgets, art content, art definitions, developers’
expenditures, the Commission has the responsibility to provide cultural witness on behalf of the city, as to the
realization of the project’s stated, mutable and ongoing goals, especially regarding Inglewood artists’ projects and
youth education programs. The Hollywood Park’s PDA was signed in 2015 and is now in its sixth year. To date, the
city has not received a prioritized plan to develop opportunities, contract artists, or identify staff to realize the
commissioning of Inglewood artists and commitment/expenditure of the $2 million dedicated for this purpose.
Director Barnes stated this is a vital aspect of the agreement. Therefore, the Inglewood Arts Commission proposes
to initiate the consultation by developing possible projects, program timelines, and funding levels for a series of public
art projects by Inglewood artists, and evaluation periods. She went on to suggest the following projects put together
by the Commission to start a conversation on how to support Inglewood artists:

Visual Public Arts
  1. Inglewood Growing Artists Projects - IGAP@HP: Open call for Inglewood artist’s proposals to be realized
  in HP public spaces. Three (3) projects over 12 months funded at $30,000 each, with support from HP
  staff.
  2. Buoyant: Inflatable or floating art at the Lake.
  3. Projectables: Original digital films projected on screens on the bridge or anchored on the lake or in the
  (free, non-ticketed) performance venues. See Film and Video Poetry Society (fvpsociety.com).

Narrative Public Art
  4. What Lies Beneath the Berm Inglewood: Augmented Reality (AR) Festival with walking tours of the berm
  perimeter; commissioned AR stories accessible through smartphones; local history, ecology, landscape
  themes.
  5. Inglewood is a Verb: Design and print three books by living Inglewood writers – fiction, non-fiction, graphic
  novel; host readings and receptions.
  6. Dramatic Readings: Professional voice artists present dramatic readings of a classic at a set time (late
  afternoon?) over four months: James Baldwin; Octavia Butler; Amanda Gorman; Octavio Paz; must seek
  permissions to perform texts at low or no fees; nominations from HP residents will be accepted.

Performed Public Art
  7. Movement Festival: Site-related performed public art: performance art, walking tours, public dance, and
  motorized sculpture).
  2
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

  8. Spoken Word: Daylong series of poets and spoken word artists.
  9. These Mighty Voices: Curated outdoor performances by local choir groups.
  10. Public Art Concerts: Free musical festival over one weekend at HP, 3 – 5 musical groups.

Director Barnes provided the following timeline:
  • 2015 – 2021: Six years of LASED planning; reported $33,500 in public art funds encumbered for
  • Inglewood artists as of 2020 report.
  • 2022: Kickoff Inglewood Growing Artists Projects with Hollywood Park (IGAP@HP)
  • 2022 – 2028: Seven years of project programming, funded at $100,000 per year ($700,000)
  • 2029: Evaluation Year – assess programming impacts and goals ($30,000 art assessment
  • Costs)
  • 2030 – 2035: Six years of project programming, funded at $120,000 per year ($720,000)

Notional Funding Information

  •  $33,500:  Reported expenditures for 2015- 2021 Planning Phase
  •  $700,000:  Phase One: Annual Public Art Commissions
  •  $30,000:  Public Art Evaluation report
  •  $720,000:  Phase Two: Annual Public Art Commissions
  •  $1,483,500 ($516,500 contingency - 25% of commitment remaining)

  Director Barnes stated the information provided is intended to spark a conversation with hopes of considering
the recommendations of the Arts Commission. Jason Witt again spoke on the 6,000 seat YouTube theater stating it’s
dedicated to public art and with the partnership of YouTube mixing the technology with local Inglewood voices could
be some cool integrations. Director Barnes stated public art being inside the theater would be wonderful but keep in
mind the art would need to be free and accessible in an un-ticketed event so that all can have access. Mr. Witt asked
with the Buoyant, were there any particular artist in mind or any suggestions from previous activities. Helen Lessick
revisited the inflatable art sculptures suggesting maybe a sculpture positioned on a float stating the overall idea is to
think broadly about what public art can be. The Notion of public art is to get it out amongst the public. Mr. Witt
thanked the Commission for taking the time to put together this well-thought-out list. Director Barnes advised Mr.
Witt that the recommendations will be submitted in writing.

  Director Barnes wanted to go back to Mr. Witt’s update to ask if the art piece he spoke on during his verbal
report would be displayed indoors or outdoors. Mr. Witt stated the piece is by Allison Sar would be displayed
outdoors at the main promenade. Director Branes asked what was happening in the performing space. Mr. Witt
answered one of the pieces by Coletta Rawls will go inside the theater, the committee recently met to discuss the
positioning of pieces. Director Barnes asked if Mr. Witt had information regarding an artist who indicted that her work
consisted of two (2) pieces and there was only an option for one (1). Mr. Witt believes that is Allison and we have a
signed agreement for the art that will be displayed in the retail store. Director Barnes asked if a timeline has been
established for her work. Mr. Witt stated the first piece should be installed in the Fall and the second piece is
expected to have a full installation by early next year. Helen Lessick asked for a description of staffing for Mr. Witt's
art program. Mr. Witt stated it is he along with team members Tracy, Kathy who are both partners on his marketing
team, and Carmen, a former art curator make up the essential committee. Jason Cannon, Managing Director, will
  3
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

make the final decisions on the placement of the art. Ms. Lessick stated that the integration of private art, purchase
artworks, and 21st Century public art is something the Arts Commission is very interested in and looking forward to
future discussions with hopes to help as a team. Commissioner Metcalf thanked Jason Witt for his update.

Staff Report

  Stephanie Maldonado introduced a staff report for receive and file with a status report regarding the Rogers
Park Artist in Residence Program, entailing the project extension, new residency dates, and a new Inglewood artist to
work in Rogers Park Community Center in three overlapping phases of creative production, community engagement,
and project evaluation. Helen Lessick gave the following update:

  •  NEA Grant extension to February 28, 2022
  •  Semi-finalist Mona Lisa Whitaker withdrew from the project on June 15, 2021
  •  Three artists were invited to submit residency exhibition proposals
  •  Each was asked to identify community engagement within the exhibit
  •  Artist Shelley Heffler was selected to update the community quilting project

  Helen Lessick shared that Shelley Heffler is a long-time Inglewood artist and her studio is located inside the
Beacon Arts Building. Ms. Heffler has spoken with the Arts Commission in the past about the Inglewood Quilt Project.
She started the project along with the South Los Angeles Gallery, creating quilt squares with individuals across Los
Angeles County under the theme “HOME”. The quilts will be auctioned off and proceeds will assist Regional
Homeless Shelters. Commissioner Metcalf and her mother participated in creating a square of their own. Ms. Heffler
has decided to create a specific Inglewood quilting project. She will set up in the Head Start room at Rogers Park with
workshops held outside. Commissioner Battle complimented Commissioner Metcalf on her square. Ms. Lessick
added that the artist also created a catalog called “We are Home” which can be found at the South Los Angeles
Gallery as well as on Shelly Heffler’s website and at Roger’s Park.
Verbal Reports

  Helen Lessick reported on regarding the following:
  • Love, Inglewood is a new portable art collection of 13 pieces created by eight (8) Inglewood
  artists. The collection is displayed throughout City Hall. On the first floor near the elevator
  banks, you will find works by Megan Reherra, Sharon, Barnes, Gail Mc Call, and Erin Goff.
  Located on the second floor in the Parking Division’s hallway, you will find artwork by Kelly
  Broomsfield-Woods, Martin Derizo, and Mina Phillips and the direct lighting installed there by
  the Inglewood Facilities Division makes the work shine. Lastly, located on the fourth floor in
  the Planning and Economic Development Department’s lobby, you will find four (4) pieces of
  art by Martin Derizo, Charles Fine, Lindsey Noble, and Evan Goff. The 13 pieces brightening
  the public areas of City Hall and we hope the public will enjoy it.
  • Skedans, The cleaning, and restoration of the monumental sculpture located outside City
  Hall by artist Tony Delap has been completed with an installation of an anti-bird railing to aid
  in preventing birds from landing on the top of the sculpture.
  4
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

Public Comments

  None

Commissioners’ Comments/Initiatives/Art Calendar

  Helen Lessick informed the Commission of the Open House at the Beckman YOLA Center on August 15,
2021, from 2:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. which will include a live concert. Both Ms. Lessick and Director Barnes were able to
tour the entire facility. Ms. Lessick stated the facility is fantastic and invited everyone to come by and see it. Director
Barnes stated that in a second meeting she and Ms. Lessick attended at Beckman YOLA, the administrative staff
indicated they will be issuing a call for instructors. If anyone knows of any instructors, please send them their way.
Commissioner Banks asked for the time of the event. Ms. Lessick stated the Open House starts at 2:00 p.m. until
5:00 p.m. and additional information can be found at www.laphil.org under Beckman YOLA’s section. Commissioner
Banks inquired about R.S.V.P. being needed. Ms. Lessick stated it’s an Open House, no R.S.V.P. is needed. Director
Barnes stated formal announcements will be made to the community to ensure the appropriate actions are being
taken such as reserving is needed especially with the current numbers of COVID-19. Ms. Lessick stated this is an
educational site gearing towards young people, masking is required.

  Helen Lessick announced the Los Angeles County Arts Commission has issued its call for the Annual
Celebration for a chance to perform at the Dorothy Chandler Pavilion on December 24, 2021. Please visit
www.holidaycelebration.org. Applications will be accepted until midnight, August 1, 2021.

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 7:13 p.m.
